questions.question: By selling an article for Rs. 640, a person loses 15% of its selling price. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell it to gain 15% on its cost price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of an article = Rs. 640

Loss = 15% of SP

Gain = 15% of CP

**Formula used:**

Gain% = (SP – CP)/CP × 100

Loss% = (CP – SP)/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

The SP of an article is Rs. 640

According to the question

CP = 640 × 15/100 + 640 = Rs. 736

Gain% = 15% = (SP – 736)/736

⇒ 736 + 0.15 × 736

⇒ 736 + 110.4

⇒ 846.40

∴ New selling price of an article is Rs. 846.40

questions.question: Find the value of (3)/(4) cot² 30 ^circ + cos² 30 ^circ - 3 cosec² 60^circ + tan² 60^circ
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 (3)/(4) cot² 30 ^circ + cos² 30 ^circ - 3 cosec² 60^circ + tan² 60^circ = ?

**Formula used:**

Cot 30° = √3

Cos 30° = √3/2

Cosec 60° = 2/√3

Tan 60° = √3

**Calculation:**

 (3)/(4) cot² 30 ^circ + cos² 30 ^circ - 3 cosec² 60^circ + tan² 60^circ 

⇒ 3/4 × (√3)² + (√3/2)² – 3 × (2/√3)² + (√3)²

⇒ 3/4 × 3 + 3/4 – 3 × 4/3 + 3

⇒ 9/4 + 3/4 – 4 + 3

⇒ 12/4 – 4 + 3

⇒ 3 – 4 + 3

⇒ 2

**So, the required value is 2**

questions.question: If x + y + z = 7, x² + y² + z² = 85 and x³ + y³ + z³ = 913, then the value of sqrt[3]{xyz} is
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x + y + z = 7

x2 + y2 + z2 = 85

x3 + y3 + z3 = 913

**Formula used:**

x³ + y³ + z³ – 3xyz = (x + y + z) (x² + y² + z² – (xy + yz + zx)) .....(1)

(x + y + z)² = x² + y² + z² + 2(xy + yz + zx) ....(2)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 7² = 85 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ 49 – 85 = 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ -36 = 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ (xy + yz + zx) = -36/2

⇒ (xy + yz + zx) =-18

⇒ 913 – 3xyz = 7(85 + 18)

⇒ 913 – 7 × 103 = 3xyz

⇒ 913 – 721 = 3xyz

⇒ 192 = 3xyz

⇒ 64 = xyz

⇒ (4)³ = sqrt[3]{xyz}

**∴ The value of sqrt[3]{xyz} is 4**

If cos(A - B) = (sqrt 3)/(2) and cot(A + B) = (1)/(sqrt 3), Where A - B and A + B are acute angles, then (2A - 3B) is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cos(A – B) = (sqrt 3)/(2)

Cot(A + B) = (1)/(sqrt 3)

**Formula used:**

Cos 30° = (sqrt 3)/(2)

Cot 60° = (1)/(sqrt 3)

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Cos(A – B) = (sqrt 3)/(2)

⇒ (A – B) = 30° ......(1)

Cot(A + B) = (1)/(sqrt 3)

⇒ (A + B) = 60° .....(2)

Now, adding both the equations we get,

⇒ (A – B) = 30° + (A + B) = 60° 

⇒ 2A = 90° 

⇒ A = 45°

Putting the value of A in equation (2)

⇒ 45° + B = 60° 

⇒ B = (60° – 45°)

⇒ B = 15° 

Now,

⇒ (2A – 3B) = (2 × 45° – 3 × 15°)

⇒ (90° – 45°)

⇒ 45° 

**So, the value of (2A - 3B) is 45° **

questions.question: A certain number of students from school X appeared in an examination and 20% students failed. From school Y, 130% more students than that from school X, appeared in the same examination. If 90% of the total number of students appeared from both the schools passed, then what is the percentage of students from school Y who failed (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Students failed in school X = 20%

Number of students in school Y = 130% more than the number of students in school X

Students passed in both school = 90%

**Calculation:**

Let the number of students in school X be 100x

Number of failed students in school X = 20% of 100x

⇒ 20x

Number of passed students in school Y = (100x – 20x) = 80x

Number of students in school Y = 100x + 130% of 100x

⇒ 100x + (130/100 × 100x)

⇒ 100x + 130x

⇒ 230x

Total number of students in school X and school Y = (100x + 230x)

⇒ 330x

Number of passes students in both school = 90% of 330x

⇒ (90/100 × 330)

⇒ 297x

So, number of passed students in school Y = (297x – 80x)

⇒ 217x

Number of failed students in school Y = (230x – 217x)

⇒ 13x

Percentage of failed students in school Y = (13x/230x) × 100

⇒ (1300x/230x)

⇒ 5.65% ~ 5.7%

**∴ The percentage of students who failed from school Y is 5.7%**

questions.question: Two men and 7 women can complete a work in 28 days whereas 6 men and 16 women can do the same work in 11 days. In how many days can 7 men complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

2 men and 7 women can complete a work = 28 days

6 men and 16 women can complete a work = 11 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

According to the question

⇒ (2m + 7w) × 28 = (6m + 16w) × 11

⇒ 56m + 196w = 66m + 176w

⇒ 10m = 20w

⇒ m/w = 2/1

Total work = (2 × 2 + 7 × 1) × 28

⇒ (4 + 7) × 28

⇒ 11 × 28

⇒ 308

Time taken by 7 men to complete the work = (308/7 × 2)

⇒ (308/14)

⇒ 22 days

**∴ Required days is 22.**

questions.question: If the seven-digit number 94x29y6 is divisible by 72, then what is the value of (2x + 3y) for x ≠ y ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Seven-digit number = 94x29y6

To be divided by 72

**Concept used:**

Divisibility rule of 8 = If the last three digits of a number are divisible by 8, then the number is completely divisible by 8

Divisibility rule of 9 = if the sum of digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number itself is divisible by 9

**Calculation:**

Now, putting the value of y = 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9, we can't divide the last 3 digit of seven-digit number by 8.

Only value of y will be 3 and 7

Now, if we take value of y as 3. Total sum of numbers should be divided by 9.

So, 9 + 4 + x + 2 + 9 + 3 + 6 = 33 + x

For sum to be divided by 9, the sum should be 36. So, value of x = 3

Now, value of both x and y = 3 which should not be the condition

So, value of y should be 7

Now, 9 + 4 + x + 2 + 9 + 7 + 6 = 37 + x

For sum to be divided by 9, the sum should be 45. So, value of x = 8

Now, Value of (2x + 3y) = (2 × 8 + 3 × 7)

⇒ 16 + 21 = 37

**∴ The required value is 37**

In a circle with centre O, PAX and PBY are the tangents to the circle at points A and B, from an external point P. Q is any point on the circle such that ∠QAX = 59° and ∠QBY = 72°. What is the measure of ∠AQB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠QAX = 59° 

∠QBY = 72° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02fc74c31a2f0933def7abe867335ca02d16d4aef8473fbabf8c9e5080a5ae60.png] 

 

 

∠OAX = 90°

⇒ ∠OAQ = 90° – (59°)

⇒ ∠OAQ = 31° 

Now, ∠OBY = 90°

⇒ ∠OBQ = 90° – (72°)

⇒ ∠OBQ = 18° 

 

Since, OB = OQ = OA

⇒ ∠OBQ = ∠OQB = 18° (radius)

⇒ ∠OAQ = ∠OQA = 31° (radius)

∠AQB = ∠OBQ + ∠OAQ

⇒ ∠AQB = (31° + 18°)

⇒ ∠AQB = 49° 

**∴ The measure of ∠AQB is 49° **
